extracted.intended_audience: religious/monastic practitioners and devout Christians seeking to advance in the interior spiritual life
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, devotional instructions for monks and devout Christians on how to live the interior life: humility, prayerful interior conversation with Christ, mortification, detachment, and preparation for judgment. The text gives concrete moral/spiritual norms and examples for daily conduct and ongoing sanctification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regardez la fin / souvenez-vous du jour du jugement
rubrics_metrics.description: «En toutes choses regardez la fin, et reportez-vous au jour où vous serez là, debout devant le Juge sévère…» — constantly keep the final judgment in mind: nothing is hidden and no excuses will avail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use continual recollection of the Last Judgment as a motive for repentance and vigilance. Imagined scene: the dead rising, secrets revealed, two cities separated — choose now because there is no repentance after death. Anti-pattern: living as if there were no future account; seeking to placate men rather than God.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purgez-vous maintenant par patience et pénitence
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a salutary purgatory here: the patient man who bears offences, prays for those who grieve him, forgives from the heart, and is ready to ask pardon if he has sinned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer present mortification and purification to paying for sins after death. Practice patient endurance of insults, interior compunction, forgiveness, and self-mortification (discipline of flesh to the spirit). Anti-pattern: flattering the flesh, delaying amendment until 'later'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mortification présente réduit le châtiment futur
rubrics_metrics.description: The more you spare and flatter your own flesh now, the more terrible your future punishment will be; man will be punished most where he most sinned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberately accept small sufferings and deny comforts now (fasting, self-denial) so as to avoid greater chastisement. Example consequences: sloth, intemperance, lust, envy, pride and avarice each have fitting torments employed as moral imagery to warn the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chaque vice a son tourment — fuir les vices particuliers
rubrics_metrics.description: Each vice has its own torment: the slothful pierced by burning goads, intemperate tormented by extreme hunger/thirst, voluptuous plunged into burning pitch and foul sulphur, envious howling like mad dogs, the proud filled with confusion, the avaricious reduced to indigence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and combat your particular predominant sins because punishment follows the specific vice. The text uses vivid images of retribution to motivate avoidance. Anti-pattern: generic remorse without targeted struggle against one's chief failing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sagesse d'être méprisable pour Jésus-Christ
rubrics_metrics.description: It will be seen that he was wise who learned to be foolish and despicable for Jesus Christ; patience in tribulation will then be applauded and iniquity silenced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer being despised, poor, or contemptible in this world for Christ's sake — these will be exalted at judgment. Valuing humility and tribulation over worldly honour/wealth is presented as a rule of judgment-worthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choisir l'amour de Dieu plutôt que les délices du monde
rubrics_metrics.description: You cannot both taste worldly delights and reign with Jesus-Christ; above all, love God and serve Him alone; if love does not yet move you, let fear restrain you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make an explicit, prioritized choice: God first. If perfect love is absent, cultivate at least filial fear of God as a restraining motive. Anti-pattern: clinging to creatures and worldly pleasures while pretending to pursue God.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vigilance et ferveur dans l'amendement de la vie
rubrics_metrics.description: Be vigilant and fervent in God's service; frequently ask why you came and why you left the world: to live for God and become a spiritual person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain ardour because present work yields eternal reward; keep firm hope but avoid complacency that leads to laxity or presumption. Practical: steady, zealous daily practice rather than spiritual indifference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agir maintenant comme si l'on était sûr de persévérer
rubrics_metrics.description: If you asked whether you would persevere, the answer is: do now what you would then do — know and do God's will now so you may enjoy peace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stop anxious curiosity about the future and focus on knowing and accomplishing God's will presently. The interior prompt 'If you knew you would persevere, what would you do?' is used as a test-action: do that now.

rubrics_metrics.name: Se vaincre soi-même: arracher les désirs et acquérir la vertu
rubrics_metrics.description: Two principal helps to amendment: violently tear yourself from what degraded nature desires and work ardently to acquire the virtue you most need.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special attention to battling the passions that trouble you most and imitating good examples; correct faults observed in others by not committing them yourself. Anti-pattern: timid or half-hearted effort; preferring easier virtues while leaving dominant vices untouched.

rubrics_metrics.name: Profiter des exemples bons et fuir les mauvais
rubrics_metrics.description: Profit from good examples and be animated to imitate them; if you see reprehensible behavior, take care not to commit the same fault and correct promptly when you have.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be watchful because others observe you as you observe them; let the sight of fervent religious spur you, and the sight of laxity cause sorrow and reparation. Practical: imitate austere discipline where observed (early rising, long prayers, poverty, silence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Méditation de la vie et de la Passion de Jésus comme école
rubrics_metrics.description: Meditate seriously on the life and Passion of the Savior; Jesus crucified should always be present to instruct and supply what is necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frequent meditative rehearsal of Christ's Passion furnishes all needed lessons and helps interior hunger for God. If you cannot reach higher contemplation, repose in the Passion and take refuge in His wounds for consolation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obéissance et fidélité à la règle; danger de tiédeur
rubrics_metrics.description: A fervent religious receives commands and submits; the lukewarm suffer continual tribulation and are deprived of interior consolations; those who abandon the rule are exposed to grave falls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe rule, accept austerity and constraint (rare outings, poor nourishment, much work, little speech, long prayers) as means to progress. Anti-pattern: seeking a less constrained life leading to anxiety and continual dissatisfaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Désirer l'oraison et la louange incessante si possible
rubrics_metrics.description: If one could praise God perpetually without need of food, drink, sleep, it would be the highest happiness; longing to be freed from bodily necessities to feed the soul alone is commended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate desire for uninterrupted interior praise and spiritual nourishment; accept bodily necessities as limitations but aspire to interior continuity of prayer. Practical example: emulate Carthusians and Cistercians rising at night to sing praises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Le royaume de Dieu est au dedans: aménager une demeure intérieure
rubrics_metrics.description: Return to God with all your heart; despise external things and give yourself to the interior so that the kingdom of God (peace and joy in the Holy Spirit) may come within you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare your heart as a dwelling for Christ: let Jesus enter and exclude all else. Interior conversation (collecting the heart) invites consolations and frequent visits from Christ. Anti-pattern: relying primarily on external devotional display rather than interior recollection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Se détacher des hommes: confiance en Dieu plutôt qu'en créatures
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not rely much on fragile mortals; men change quickly — put your trust wholly in God, who remains constant and will care for you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let God be both fear and love; accept that no stable earthly dwelling exists here and that intimacy with Christ is the only true rest. Practical stance: expect change in human relations and anchor yourself in God.

rubrics_metrics.name: Préparer le coeur pour l'Époux — exclusive dévotion au Christ
rubrics_metrics.description: Hasten to prepare your heart for the Spouse (Christ); if you possess Jesus you are rich and need nothing else; give Him sole possession of your interior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude every rival affection so Christ may dwell within; once interior possession of Christ is achieved, earthly consolation loses power to disturb. Practical: aim for singular attachment to Christ.

rubrics_metrics.name: S'abandonner à Dieu en esprit d'humilité
rubrics_metrics.description: Be little concerned who is for or against you; ensure God is with you in all you do. Humble acknowledgement of faults calms others and brings God's favor; silence and suffering are useful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate a pure conscience and practice silence and patient endurance of reproach; consider reproaches as aids to humility. Anti-pattern: pride that cannot bear correction and seeks to answer every accusation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conserver la paix intérieure et rendre la paix aux autres
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep peace first within yourself so you can impart it to others. The peaceable person restores good where passion and suspicion create trouble.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize self-correction over judging others; be patient with the harsh, perverse, or disagreeable — living peacefully with such persons is a great grace. Anti-pattern: a temperament that stirs up suspicion, speaks imprudently, neglects personal duties while judging others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicité d'intention et pureté d'affection
rubrics_metrics.description: Man rises above earth on two wings: simplicity (in intention) and purity (in affection). Simplicity seeks God; purity finds and tastes Him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to will only what God wills and what is useful to neighbor; inner freedom from disordered affections makes every good work easier. A pure heart perceives spiritual realities clearly; if you fall into tepidity, engage in renewed mortification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Se regarder soi-même plutôt que juger autrui
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not rely on yourself; you have little light and are often blind within. Prefer caring for yourself and maintaining silence about others rather than exposing or judging them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-knowledge is the true study: learn to despise yourself, lament the plague of self-love, and work toward interior reformation. Practical: cease prying into or criticizing others; focus on remedying your own faults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conserver une bonne conscience comme source de joie
rubrics_metrics.description: The glory of the good man is the testimony of his conscience: keep conscience pure to possess abiding joy even in adversities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not seek the fleeting praise of men; true glory is inward and founded on suffering with the Cross. Be content whether praised or blamed; God sees the heart and intentions. Anti-pattern: craving human honour as a measure of spiritual worth.
